digest.definition: Two related degrees told apart: Biomedical Science (singular), built to the professional body's accreditation requirements and covering every clinical laboratory specialism, and Biomedical Sciences (plural), broader and reaching into other human biology, including named awards such as pharmacology, molecular or cell biology
distinctiveFeatures: Two related degrees told apart: Biomedical Science (singular), built to the professional body's accreditation requirements and covering every clinical laboratory specialism, and Biomedical Sciences (plural), broader and reaching into other human biology, including named awards such as pharmacology, molecular or cell biology
Its object is the scientific basis of human health and disease, from molecules and cells to whole systems

The singular degree is the academic step towards registration as a Biomedical Scientist, a protected title; with verified clinical training, it leads to work in NHS and private diagnostic pathology laboratories
Hands-on laboratory work is essential, giving technical skill and safe, accurate practice in clinical, industrial and research laboratories
Research skills, critical appraisal and independent investigation run through the courses and prepare for employment or research degrees
Related courses in the area, Pharmacology, Human Nutrition and Physiology, share a common core and have their own content and accrediting bodies
A systems-led approach integrates the clinical specialisms with the underlying science of investigation and treatment

subjectSpecific.text: On this course you will come to know how normal cells and tissues are built, at gross and fine scale, and how disease alters that structure.
On this course you will come to know reproductive science, with infertility and the study of embryos.
On this course you will come to know how cells and tissues are prepared for examination under the microscope.
On this course you will come to know the principles and uses of imaging and visualisation methods, microscopy among them, in supporting diagnosis and the choice of treatment.
On this course you will come to know the common methods for collecting clinical samples and analysing them.
On this course you will come to know how the main body and organ systems are investigated, for example through kidney, liver, bone profile and tumour marker tests.
On this course you will come to know the principles and uses of biochemical tests in screening for disease, diagnosing it, treating it and following its course.
On this course you will come to know monitoring of therapeutic drugs and the investigation of substance misuse.
On this course you will come to know how the effectors of the immune response work and how they are measured.

On this course you will come to know why immune function goes wrong and what follows, neoplastic disease and transplant reactions included, and how these are detected, diagnosed, treated and followed.
On this course you will come to know the principles and practice of immunological methods in screening, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, with prophylaxis and immunotherapy.
On this course you will come to know how blood cells are formed, built and work.
On this course you will come to know how normal haemostasis is regulated.
On this course you will come to know the appearance of blood cells: recognising normal white cells and the usual red cell abnormalities.
On this course you will come to know the nature and diagnosis of anaemias, blood cancers and disorders of bleeding and thrombosis.
On this course you will come to know the principles and practice of haematology methods in screening, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
On this course you will come to know interpreting blood groups, the causes of grouping anomalies, and screening for antibodies.
On this course you will come to know the genetics, inheritance, structure and role of antigens on red cells.
On this course you will come to know the destruction of blood cells by the immune system.
On this course you will come to know how blood components are prepared, stored and used.
On this course you will come to know patient blood management.
On this course you will come to know choosing suitable blood components for transfusion, and the adverse effects that can follow.
On this course you will come to know genomic, transcriptomic and proteomic methods for analysing human chromosomes and DNA.
On this course you will come to know how molecular biology and bioinformatics are applied in medicine.
On this course you will come to know pharmacogenetics and personalised medicine.
On this course you will come to know the principles and practice of genetic testing in screening, diagnosis and follow-up, and the ethical questions it raises.
On this course you will come to know the mechanisms by which a range of microorganisms cause disease.
On this course you will come to know public health microbiology, the epidemiology and control of infection, and the One Health concept.

On this course you will come to know the principles and practice of methods for screening, diagnosing, treating and following infectious diseases, for detecting and identifying microorganisms, and for preventing and controlling infection, vaccination and environmental and vector control included.
On this course you will come to know antimicrobial chemotherapy and resistance to antibiotics, antivirals, antifungals and anti-parasitic drugs.
On this course you will come to know the principles and uses of investigations run on near-patient testing equipment for screening, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
On this course you will come to know how near-patient testing fits into patient pathways.
On this course you will come to know the quality assurance points that bear on near-patient testing.
On this course you will come to know how to interpret quality control standards.
On this course you will come to know why quality assurance and pre-analytical variables matter.
On this course you will come to know why external quality assessment matters.

On this course you will come to know quality management at a basic level: quality policy, audit, standard operating procedures, training and competency records, error and incident reporting, validation and verification, and reagent stock.
On this course you will come to know laboratory accreditation, with a basic awareness of UKAS and ISO standards.
On this course you will come to know the molecular targets drugs act on, such as receptors, enzymes, ion channels and transporters.
On this course you will come to know how drugs relate to receptors, covering agonism and antagonism, specificity and selectivity, potency, desensitisation and tolerance.
On this course you will come to know the structure and function of the main drug targets and how drugs change that function at molecular level.
On this course you will come to know how drugs act on the major organ systems and on cell function, proliferation and death.
On this course you will come to know pharmacokinetics, what the body does to drugs: their absorption, distribution, biotransformation and excretion.

On this course you will come to know why people differ in drug response and toxicity, through ethnicity, gender, age, pregnancy, genes, disease and drug interactions, and the emerging technologies of personalised medicine.
On this course you will come to know how drug concentration or dose relates to response.

On this course you will come to know experimental methods used in pharmacology, such as bioassays, receptor binding and cloning, therapeutic recombinant proteins, animal disease models and genetic manipulation.
On this course you will come to know the ethics and law of using animals in research, and ways to replace, refine and reduce that use.
On this course you will come to know how drugs are discovered and developed, toxicology included, and the regulation that oversees their quality, safety and effectiveness.
On this course you will come to know the principles of clinical trials (bias, sample size, the placebo effect, therapeutic index) and the ethics of using human participants and tissues.
On this course you will come to know the chemistry of life, how nutrients work in the main metabolic pathways, and the cellular and molecular roots of disease, gene expression included.
On this course you will come to know the clinical biochemistry of human disease and how it is managed, weighted towards nutritional factors.
On this course you will come to know how nutritional status is assessed, the main nutritional issues at each life stage, and how socio-demographic, economic and environmental factors shape diet.
On this course you will come to know the ideas and processes of food science, safety, storage, processing and microbiology.
On this course you will come to know clinical nutrition, diet therapy, health promotion and nutrition education.
On this course you will come to know nutrition for sport and exercise performance.
On this course you will come to know how genes and nutrients interact and what that may mean for preventing diet-related disease.
On this course you will come to know how nutritional status bears on disease, and a core theoretical sense that human disease and its care draw on many disciplines.
On this course you will come to know the levels of organisation from chemical to whole organism, and the internal and external factors that regulate body systems.
On this course you will come to know how structure relates to function in each body system, what each system fundamentally does and how the systems interrelate.
On this course you will come to know the processes of life: metabolism, responsiveness, movement, growth, differentiation and reproduction.
On this course you will come to know the systems by which cells communicate with each other.
On this course you will come to know homeostasis, both self-regulation and regulation from outside the organ.
On this course you will come to know neural tissue, the spinal cord, spinal nerves and reflexes, the brain, cranial nerves and neural integration.
On this course you will come to know the balance of fluids, electrolytes, acids and bases, its control, its disturbances and their effect on health.
On this course you will come to know the endocrine system: how hormones are secreted and distributed and how they act.
On this course you will come to know how the body responds to internal and external stressors.
On this course you will come to know how neuronal, hormonal and chemical signals coordinate and integrate the work of body systems.
On this course you will come to know how physiological responses and regulation allow adaptation and survival as the environment changes.
On this course you will come to know the main parts of a human cell, its chief transport processes and how it keeps itself intact.
On this course you will come to know how cells differentiate and cycle, the variety of cell types, and the intracellular chemistry that sustains life and drives cell responses.
On this course you will come to know the structure and function of epithelial and connective tissues and membranes, and how tissues are injured and repaired.
On this course you will come to know the basics of skin, bone structure, the skeleton and joints.
On this course you will come to know skeletal muscle and the other kinds of muscle tissue.
On this course you will come to know exercise physiology, the effects of exercise and the nutrition linked to it.
On this course you will come to know the cardiovascular system: blood and haemostasis, the heartbeat and cardiodynamics, and cardiovascular physiology and its regulation.
On this course you will come to know the lymphatic system, its organisation, defences and immunity.
On this course you will come to know the respiratory system and its physiology.
On this course you will come to know the digestive and hepatobiliary systems: their organs and the processes of digestion, absorption, detoxification and elimination.

statements.about: applying leading-edge understanding to complex problems
statements.paraphrase: In addition to the honours outcomes, master's graduates should be able to develop, combine, synthesise and apply a systematic, broad understanding of current and leading-edge biomedical concepts to solve complex problems.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students should be able to bring a systematic, broad and current understanding of biomedical concepts to bear on complex problems, on top of the honours outcomes.

statements.appliesTo: master's graduates in Biomedical Science or Biomedical Sciences
statements.about: research from the literature to a significant project
statements.paraphrase: Master's graduates should be able to interrogate and combine varied scientific literature and other information to design and develop methods of investigation and analysis, at the forefront and beyond their own specialism; this takes in planning a project (ethics, hazards, environmental effects, sustainability and costs, as fits), building advanced experimental and investigative skills, and discussing the background, context, methods, results and likely impact of a substantial research project.

forPractitioner.text: At master's level, students should be able to design investigations from a critical synthesis of the literature, plan a project with its ethics, hazards, environmental and cost aspects, develop advanced experimental skills and discuss a substantial research project in full.

forBeneficiary.text: On a master's course you should become able to draw on a wide range of scientific literature to design your own methods, plan a substantial research project with its ethical, safety, environmental and cost aspects, build advanced laboratory and investigative skills, and discuss your project's background, methods, results and impact.
